finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: User input is directly sent to the server without validation
finding.assumptions: The server might execute the received data as a command

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is sendto, which only transmits data over the network and does not invoke any shell or system call. The data sent is an int, not a string that could be interpreted as a command. No command execution occurs in this code fragment, so OS Command Injection cannot be triggered from the client side.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: User input is directly read into an integer without validation
finding.assumptions: The input might be larger than the expected integer size

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the source is scanf("%d", &number) which writes directly into an int variable. The sink is sendto(client_socket, &number, sizeof(int), …) which sends exactly sizeof(int) bytes. No buffer larger than the destination is used, and no bounds checks are required. The reported issue describes an integer overflow, not a buffer overflow, and the code does not expose a buffer overflow path.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Received data is directly printed without validation
finding.assumptions: The received data might be crafted to exploit the server

parsed.refutation_attempt: The data received via recvfrom is stored in an int variable 'number' and printed using a constant format string "%d". Since the format string is not influenced by user input and the argument is an integer, there is no possibility of OS command injection. The source (recvfrom) is neutralised by the type conversion to int and the sink (printf) is safe because it uses a fixed format string.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Received data is directly printed without validation
finding.assumptions: The received data might be crafted to exploit the server

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is printf with a fixed format string "%d\n" and the argument is an int variable 'number' that is filled by recvfrom. Since the format string is constant and the argument type is integer, there is no possibility of command injection or format string exploitation. The data received from recvfrom is treated as a binary integer, not as a string that could be interpreted by the shell. Therefore the reported OS Command Injection claim is invalid.
